elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits Customer to terminate the Agreement during the Term for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires at least 90 days' written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no pro-rata refund obligation.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: M&I's convenience-based withdrawal of non-Core Services under Section 10.2 may take effect only at the end of the Term; the immediate-termination language is tied to a regulatory, legislative, or judicial trigger rather than convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits convenience termination on at least 90 days' written notice.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination for Convenience Fee equals three months of Customer's average monthly Fees, and the additional unamortized costs and disposition expenses were removed.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 allows M&I's unilateral withdrawal of non-Core Services to become effective only at the end of the Term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 requires M&I to provide 90 days' prior written notice for its end-of-Term withdrawal right.
